## Highlights

- Experimental native Windows Sandbox runs PowerShell and file operations inside MXC, with broad disk reads and workspace-confined writes by default.
- App-owned local Envd runtime management, opt-in desktop access, interactive resource monitoring, and reorganized Settings improve local environment setup and visibility.

## Upgrade notes

Harness UI requires Harness and Stream Protocol `>=0.14.0,<0.15.0` and `a13n-envd-client>=0.4.0,<0.5.0`. Managed Local EIP downloads the daemon matching the installed client version; upgrading UI alone while retaining an older pinned client is not a supported combination. Explicit executable overrides and custom endpoints must be upgraded separately.

## Known issues

- Native Windows Sandbox requires a supported MXC/PSEC host and remains experimental. Its default broad-read policy includes account-accessible Host configuration and disk credentials; it confines writes rather than providing Host-file confidentiality.
- Node.js 24.21 `fs.realpathSync.native` can return `EPERM` under MXC. PowerShell, Git, and Python passed focused native acceptance; other toolchains need validation on the target Windows build.
